title: Butterfly Effect Launches Manus2.0: Costs Drop by 30%, Agents Can Also Team Up for Work
excerpt: After independent operation adjustments, Butterfly Effect Company has officially launched the overseas version of Manus 2.0 with a major update. Unlike current
content_html:
After independent operation adjustments, Butterfly Effect Company has officially launched the overseas version of Manus 2.0 with a major update. Unlike current mainstream AI products that focus on conversational abilities, Manus 2.0 places its core emphasis on "task execution," aiming to make AI truly become users' digital assistants.

According to official information, Manus 2.0 has undergone a comprehensive upgrade in its underlying architecture. The new framework reduces task execution time by nearly 30% and cuts operational costs by about one-third. This means users can complete more complex AI tasks with a smaller budget.

In terms of features, the most notable change in Manus 2.0 is its "remote assistance" capability. Users only need to set up trigger conditions, and the AI can automatically start workflows upon receiving emails or calendar reminders. From cloud file retrieval to format conversion, Manus 2.0 can directly operate on the server side without requiring users to be online in real time.

In the content creation field, Manus 2.0 significantly lowers the barriers to video and game production. Users just need to provide a creative direction, and the AI can create a preliminary video draft, supporting manual refinement; in game development, users can choose templates, customize characters, and even deploy multiplayer online servers with one click.

Additionally, Manus 2.0 has introduced an Agent collaboration application called Cue. Multiple AI Agents can form a "work group" in Cue, each with its own email and wallet, capable of sending messages to each other, collaborating on tasks, and even answering calls or ordering food via QR code scanning on behalf of users.
